answer: Mutual-stake handshakes: two agents lock equal deposits in a bilateral escrow before trading, and either side can trigger arbitration if cheated. Like pigment mixing only when two tubes are squeezed together, the bond activates only when both commit real capital. A willow bends with its partner tree; a lone cedar stands isolated and untrusted. A sybil farmer can pair fakes with fakes, but every arbitration burns real deposits, and running a thousand fake pairs means a thousand real escrows bleeding capital — collusion leaves a ledger trail of burned bonds no farmer can hide.
